{
    "content": "<p>I'm just about finished backing everything up off of my main machine (Windows 7\n32-bit Ultimate). I've heard alot of good things about Windows 7 (read quite a\nbit too) - and even decent things about the install process. What's tying me to\nWindows is Fallout 3 and the random Windows-only game...sorry Ubuntu, I love ya'\nbut we just can't go steady yet.</p>\n<p>I'll update this post as I install and use this new OS. It feels like getting a new\ncomputer!</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Update 2:41pm</strong> - I started the install at 2:20 and am typing this from the same machine with Windows 7 now. Checking the device manager, I've got only 1 device (my ATI TV tuner...don't buy one of\nthese) not recognized. Next up - Video drivers, TV Tuner drivers, and some\napps.</li>\n<li><strong>Update 3:16pm</strong> - It looks like my ATI TV tuner doesn't have a listed driver available for Windows 7. Some searching revealed that some had success with using the Vista 64 bit driver from the\n<a href=\"http://support.amd.com/us/gpudownload/Pages/index.aspx\">ATI downloads page</a>. I installed this driver, but the device manager still showed the unknown device. Choosing to &quot;Update driver&quot;, I pointed the wizard to the\nlocation that the ATI installer had unpacked all the files to (C:\\ATI). Windows\npicked up the driver and it's now listed as &quot;ATI Unified AVStream Driver&quot;. I'm\nstill configuring Windows Media Center, so I'm not sure if this will all work\nout - but the driver installed fine.</li>\n<li><strong>Update 3:50pm</strong> - TV Tuner works fine. Getting signal out here in the stix is\nanother matter :)</li>\n<li><strong>Update 5:47pm</strong> - Got some of my apps installed. Restored Fallout 3 from the\nbackup I created back into Steam - only to have to do the Games for Windows Live\ndance (don't update through the game, go get the standalone client). Oh - and\ndoing a steam backup of the game doesn't capture any downloadable content you've\nacquired through GFWL. Bummer... at my current internet speed rate - I should be\nable to play Fallout 3 sometime next week.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>Overall at this point I'm liking Windows 7. The real test comes tonight when I reshare my printer to\nanother Windows XP box in the house. Vista was <em>terrible</em> with this...I had to restart\nthe print spooler and open the printers window every time that machine needed to\nprint. Here's hoping it's gotten better in 7.</p>\n<p><strong>Update 10/25/2009</strong> - It's been a good while since I installed and I haven't\nlonged for XP or Vista at all. Printer sharing worked fantastic! No more\nrestarting the print spooler. Fallout 3 finished installing and it ran the\nhardware check to auto-set my video settings. It auto-set higher settings than\nmy Vista install did - now I can see NPCs faces :) Good times.</p>\n",
